picks.file: Civitates orbis terrarum. Urbium praecipuarum totius mundi. Liber quartus (page 86).jpg
picks.what: Bird’s-eye view across the Oder, engraving in Braun and Hogenberg, Civitates Orbis Terrarum, vol. 4
picks.why: hand-colored 1594 copy of the vol. 4 plate, largest scan; walled town, castle, bridge and Oder; book margins cut

picks.file: Ludwig Eduard Lütke - Stettin - Blick von der Lastadie-Oderinsel 1836.jpg
picks.what: The ducal castle seen across the harbor from the Lastadie, painting
picks.why: color view of the river front with the castle towers; date in title and date field agree

picks.file: General view and Great Bridge, Stettin, Germany-LCCN2002696191.jpg
picks.what: St. James’s Church and the Long Bridge over the Oder, photochrom print (Library of Congress)
picks.why: color river-front view with the cathedral spire; LoC master of the same print as #22; border and caption cut

picks.file: Szczecin PCP i Jasne Blonia dron (1).jpg
picks.what: Jasne Błonia park with the city skyline beyond, aerial photograph
picks.why: recognizable central Szczecin scene, city hall and towers behind; the other P6 drone shots are outer suburbs

gaps: P0: no candidates; P2: only flat Merian fortification plans (#9, #10); P5: nothing usable
notes: Braun and Hogenberg year set to vol. 4 (1588) rather than the 1594 copy date; #7 is a brighter colored copy but only 1407 px. Skipped #15 (Most, finer and larger P3 painting, but date field says 1847 and file name 1857), #14 (file name 1836, date field 1839) and #12 (dated only 1830–1870). #11 is a good pre-war aerial postcard with St. James’s spire, but undated (‘1720’ is a card number), so skipped. #26 (port aerial, ‘likely around 1920’) and the 1944 vertical aerials are not city views. #33 (2014 high-altitude aerial of the whole city) is an alternative for P6 but dark and without recognizable landmarks.
